reports.note_on_ambiguity: Unresolvable conflict between narrative and statistical tables. The narrative 'Hot Topics' section reports 7,838 BEC complaints with losses of over $263 million. However, the '2015 Crime Types' table later in the report lists Business Email Compromise with different totals (approx. $246 million). Both data points are documented here as per the ambiguity rules.

The report groups Business Email Compromise (BEC) and Email Account Compromise (EAC) into a single combined category ('BEC/EAC') throughout both the narrative ('Hot Topics') and the statistical tables ('2016 Crime Types'). It is not possible to isolate the exact incident counts or financial loss corresponding exclusively to Organizational Spear Phishing (BEC).

The report groups Business Email Compromise (BEC) and Email Account Compromise (EAC) into a single combined category ('BEC/EAC'). The 'Hot Topics for 2017' section cites 15,690 complaints and $675 million in losses for this combined category. It is not possible to isolate the figures corresponding exclusively to Organizational Spear Phishing (BEC).

The report groups Business Email Compromise (BEC) and Email Account Compromise (EAC) into a single combined category ('BEC/EAC'). The report cites 20,373 complaints and adjusted losses of over $1.2 billion (approx. $1.298 billion in statistical tables) for this combined category. It is not possible to isolate the figures corresponding exclusively to Organizational Spear Phishing (BEC).

The report groups Business Email Compromise (BEC) and Email Account Compromise (EAC) into a single combined category ('BEC/EAC'). The report cites 23,775 complaints and $1,776,549,688 in losses for this combined category. It is not possible to isolate the figures corresponding exclusively to Organizational Spear Phishing (BEC).

The report's narrative indicates 19,369 complaints and an adjusted loss of approximately $1.8 billion for BEC/EAC. It continues the trend of grouping Business Email Compromise (BEC) and Email Account Compromise (EAC) into a single combined category, preventing the isolation of figures corresponding exclusively to Organizational Spear Phishing (BEC).

The report's narrative states there were 19,954 complaints and adjusted losses of nearly $2.4 billion for the combined category of BEC/EAC. The exact figure exclusively for Organizational Spear Phishing (BEC) cannot be isolated because of this grouping.

Starting in 2022, the IC3 renamed the combined 'BEC/EAC' category to simply 'Business Email Compromise' (BEC). However, this broad category still functionally encompasses both organizational and personal email compromises. The report cites 21,832 complaints and over $2.7 billion in adjusted losses. It is still not possible to isolate the figures corresponding exclusively to Organizational Spear Phishing.

The report indicates 21,489 complaints and approximately $2.9 billion in reported losses for Business Email Compromise (BEC). Consistent with the methodology established in 2022, this simplified category still functionally encompasses personal Email Account Compromise (EAC) incidents. It remains impossible to isolate the figures corresponding exclusively to Organizational Spear Phishing.

The report lists 21,442 complaints and $2,770,151,146 in losses under 'Business Email Compromise'. Consistent with the methodology established in recent years, this category is understood to encompass both organizational (BEC) and personal email compromise (EAC). It remains impossible to isolate the figures corresponding exclusively to Organizational Spear Phishing.

The report lists 24,768 complaints and $3,046,598,558 in losses under 'Business Email Compromise'. Consistent with the methodology established since 2022, this category is understood to encompass both organizational (BEC) and personal email compromise (EAC). It remains impossible to isolate the figures corresponding exclusively to Organizational Spear Phishing.
